name: people
label: People
description: HR, recruiting, people operations, total rewards and learning roles.
sources: the government, the regulator or the professional body for the country
dimensions: The policy or practice, and why it exists
Legal and compliance points for the country
Fairness, consistency and records
How the people involved are treated and told
Risks, and when to escalate or take advice
How success is measured (for example retention, time to hire, engagement)
Where you have done it

name: design
label: Design
description: Product, UX, UI, service and content designers, and design researchers.
sources: accessibility standards bodies, government design guidance and the documentation of the tools the role uses
dimensions: Who the users are and what problem they have
How you learned it (research methods and evidence)
The options you explored, and why you chose one
Accessibility and inclusion
How the design was tested, and what changed because of it
Working with product, engineering and stakeholders
Where you have done it

name: strategy
label: Strategy
description: Strategy, business analysis, consulting and corporate development roles.
sources: official statistics, regulators and the published reports of the companies concerned
dimensions: The question to answer, and how it is structured
The facts and assumptions, and which ones matter most
The options, and how they compare (value, cost, risk)
A clear recommendation and what would change it
How it gets carried out, and who has to agree
How success is measured
Where you have done it

name: product
label: Product
description: Product managers and product owners, and product-minded analytics roles.
sources: the documentation of the products and tools the role uses, and regulators where the product is regulated
dimensions: The user problem, and who has it
How success is measured, and why those measures
What goes first, and what is left out
Trade-offs and risks, and how to test them cheaply
Working with engineering, design and stakeholders
Where you have done it
A clear recommendation and the next step

name: delivery
label: Delivery
description: Project, program and delivery managers, and scrum masters.
sources: the standards bodies and professional associations for the method
dimensions: Scope, goals and what done means
The plan: milestones, dependencies and the critical path
Risks and issues: how they are found, owned and escalated
Stakeholders and communication
The method chosen (agile, phased or a mix) and why
Budget, people and the trade-offs between scope, time and cost
Where you have done it

name: finance
label: Finance
description: Finance, accounting, audit, tax and financial planning roles.
sources: the accounting standards board, the tax authority and the regulator for the country
dimensions: The rule, standard or process, and why it exists
How the numbers are produced and checked (controls, reconciliations, approvals)
Rules and compliance for the country
Judgment calls and how they are documented
Risks and how they are reported
How it is measured and improved (accuracy, timeliness, cost)
Where you have done it

name: sales-marketing
label: Sales and marketing
description: Sales, account management, customer success, marketing and communications roles.
sources: advertising and consumer-protection regulators, and the documentation of the tools the role uses
dimensions: The customer or audience, and what they need
The approach and the message, and why
How it is measured (pipeline, conversion, retention, reach) and the targets
What did not work, and what changed because of it
Working with product, finance and other teams
Rules that apply (consumer protection, privacy, advertising)
Where you have done it

name: operations
label: Operations
description: Operations, supply chain, back-office and customer-support roles.
sources: the regulator and the standards bodies for the industry and country
dimensions: The process: inputs, steps, outputs and owners
Controls and accuracy (checks, reconciliations, approvals)
Rules and compliance for the country
The tools and systems used, and their limits
How it is measured (for example cycle time, error rate, cost) and improved
Handling exceptions and escalations
Where you have done it

name: engineering
label: Engineering
description: Software, data, cloud, infrastructure, security and architecture roles: frontend, backend, platform, data engineering, architecture.
sources: the vendor's own documentation and the standards bodies for the technology
dimensions: What it is and the problem it solves
When to choose it, and the alternatives (why not those)
Key limits and gotchas
Security (identity, encryption, exposure)
Cost drivers
Scaling and failure behavior (regions and zones, limits, quotas)
Where you have used it
What changed in the last 3 years, and anything deprecated
